Below the ray w stays bounded and x is squeezed between reciprocal affine functions of time, so the solution is global and x→0; the invariant forces w→0. Integrating (1/x)'→a yields tx→1/a and the invariant gives the stated y-amplitude with exponent 1+1/P=b/a. The ray solves x'=−γx². Above the ray dt/dw=w^(−P−1)(w−w_*)^(ν−1)/(kH_+); the upper tail has exponent −1−φ and y tends to infinity, so the integrable upper endpoint is the maximal lifetime. The change to s=w_*/w reverses integration limits and yields (4). The invariant gives xy^(b/c)→H_+^(k/c), and (1/y)'→−c gives (5). Since B−B_s=(1−s)^ν/ν+O((1−s)^(ν+1)), subtracting exactly the full w_0-dependent profile in (7) gives −1/(kνw_*x_0)=−1/(γx_0); subtracting only the leading power would not in general give that finite part. ν is positive, continuous on a connected rate region, and approaches both zero and infinity on that region. The reflection formula gives B(1/3,5/3)=4π/(3√3) and substitution reproduces both constants in (8).
